sider.p: Sussi is a small design system by NotlandDesign: design tokens, CSS and React components, built for WCAG 2.2 AA in light and dark. This page takes you from nothing to a page with a button, a dialog and a toast, in your own colours. Every example is a complete HTML file you can save and open.

sider.p: Every component in Sussi, grouped as in the code. Each page has an example, the props, accessibility and content.

Buttons. The button is the ordinary action in Sussi: one primary per view, secondary and ghost for the rest. Five variants (primary, secondary, soft, ghost, danger), three sizes (30, 38 and 46 px), an icon before or after the text, and a loading state that swaps the icon for a spinner and turns the button off without losing focus. It renders as a link with as="a".

h.p: The types are in components/buttons/Button.d.ts. The card with every variant, size and state:…

sider.p: Buttons. A square button with only an icon, for toolbars, row actions and the corner of a dialog. label is required and becomes both aria-label and title, so the button always has a name. Three variants (ghost, secondary, primary), three sizes (30, 38, 46 px) and round for floating actions.

h.p: The types are in components/buttons/IconButton.d.ts. The card: components/buttons/buttons.card.html (the "icon" row).

sider.p: Buttons. A button that opens the file chooser. It looks like Button, with the same variants and sizes, but is a <label class="s-btn"> around a visually hidden <input type="file">. The input stays in the tab order, so Tab lands on it and the label shows the focus ring. onFiles gets the files picked, and the input is reset after each pick.

h.p: The types are in components/buttons/FileButton.d.ts. The card: components/buttons/filebutton.card.html.
The behaviour is tested in tests/filebutton.e2e.test.mjs, the rules in tests/filebutton.test.mjs.

sider.p: Controls. A checkbox for independent yes/no choices and task lists. A native <input type="checkbox"> inside a <label>, with a drawn box (18 px, 5 px corners) that fills with the accent when checked, an optional description under the text, and indeterminate for "some of these".

h.p: The types are in components/controls/Checkbox.d.ts. The card with Checkbox, Radio and Switch:…

sider.p: Controls. A radio button for one choice among two to five visible options. A native <input type="radio"> inside a <label>, with a round box that gets an accent dot when selected, and an optional description under the text. Several Radios with the same name form a group, and the browser keeps exactly one selected.

h.p: The types are in components/controls/Radio.d.ts. The card: components/controls/controls.card.html.

sider.p: Controls. A toggle for settings that apply at once, with no save button. A native <input type="checkbox" role="switch"> inside a <label>, with a 34 × 20 px track that fills with the accent when on, and a thumb that slides across. label and description as in Checkbox.

h.p: The types are in components/controls/Switch.d.ts. The card: components/controls/controls.card.html.

sider.p: Display. A small pill that shows a status, a version or a count, and cannot be pressed. Seven tones (neutral, accent, success, warning, danger, info, clay) as a soft background with dark text, an optional leading dot, outline for a transparent variant with an edge, and mono for numbers and versions. The pill sizes itself to the text.

h.p: The types are in components/display/Badge.d.ts. The card with Badge, Tag and Card: components/display/display.card.html.

sider.p: Display. A surface that holds content that belongs together. outlined by default: --surface-1, a 1 px --border and 14 px corners, no shadow, because borders carry structure in Sussi and a shadow only means "lifted". raised swaps the border for --shadow-md for things that float, sunken is --surface-2 without a border for wells and quotes. Four paddings (none, sm 12, md 20, lg 32 px) and interactive for a card that can be pressed.

h.p: The types are in components/display/Card.d.ts. The specimen card: components/display/display.card.html.

sider.p: Display. A pill-shaped chip for filters, categories and removable selections. Without onClick it is a <span> with an edge; with selected or onClick it becomes a toggle button (aria-pressed) that fills with the soft accent when selected. onRemove adds a separate remove button (×, 24 px) beside the text, never inside the toggle, named "Fjern <text>" by default.

h.p: The types are in components/display/Tag.d.ts. The card with Badge, Tag and Card: components/display/display.card.html.
The behaviour is tested in tests/forms.e2e.test.mjs.

sider.p: Display. A row that opens something: a project, a recipe, a plant. With href it is a link, with onClick a button, and with neither a plain row. In front sits an icon (a 40 px square) or an image (48 × 48), then the title and a meta line, and at the end a chevron when the row opens something. At least 56 px tall, with a fixed lead column so the titles line up in a list that mixes icons and images.

h.p: The types are in components/display/ListItem.d.ts. The card: components/display/listitem.card.html.
The behaviour is tested in tests/listitem.e2e.test.mjs.

sider.p: Display. A row that scrolls sideways without a scrollbar and fades at the edge where there is more to see. The children sit on one line (display:flex, no wrap, an 8 px gap from --scrollrow-gap), and the row sets data-fade-start and data-fade-end by where you are. With label it is a named region that takes focus, so the keyboard can scroll it when the content has nothing to focus itself. scrollEdges is the arithmetic behind the fade, exported for tests and for apps that draw their own.

h.p: The types are in components/display/ScrollRow.d.ts. The card, shared with Swatch: components/display/swatch.card.html.
The behaviour is tested in tests/nye.e2e.test.mjs.

sider.p: Display. A colour dot: the colour of a garment, a flower, a project. Without onClick it is a plain dot, named by label or hidden from screen readers without one. With onClick it is a toggle button (aria-pressed) with a 44 px target and a ring when selected. A hex colour under 3:1 against the page gets a firmer edge in that theme, so white shows on light and black on dark.

h.p: The types are in components/display/Swatch.d.ts. The card, shared with ScrollRow: components/display/swatch.card.html.
The behaviour is tested in tests/nye.e2e.test.mjs.

sider.p: Feedback. What a list or a page shows when there is nothing in it yet. An icon in a 56 px soft accent circle, a heading, one calm line on what to do next, and at most one action, usually a Button. Centred, with the text capped at 30 characters wide. The heading level is the page's to choose (level, default h2), and framed draws it as a card when it sits among other cards.

h.p: The types are in components/feedback/EmptyState.d.ts. The card: components/feedback/emptystate.card.html.
The behaviour is tested in tests/nye.e2e.test.mjs.

sider.p: Feedback. How far something has come: a bar (plants watered, an upload) or a ring (a session, with the number in the middle). role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/min/max; without value it is indeterminate, with no valuenow and a calm sweep that becomes a fade under prefers-reduced-motion. The fill is the accent or a status colour, the track is --surface-3 with a --border-control edge, so track and fill hold 3:1 in both themes and every accent.

h.p: The types are in components/feedback/Progress.d.ts. The card: components/feedback/progress.card.html.
The behaviour is tested in tests/progress.e2e.test.mjs, the colour rules in tests/progress.test.mjs.

sider.p: Feedback. The box at the top of a form after a failed submit, as GOV.UK and Designsystemet do it: a title, an optional line and one link per field with an error. It takes the focus when it appears, so people hear what went wrong and the page scrolls to it; each link moves the focus to its field, or to the first control in a Fieldset. The app owns the list: mount the box when the submit fails, remove it when the form is valid.

h.p: The types are in components/feedback/ErrorSummary.d.ts. The card: components/feedback/errorsummary.card.html.
The behaviour is tested in tests/errorsummary.e2e.test.mjs, the colour rules in tests/errorsummary.test.mjs.

sider.p: Feedback. A message that stays on the page until the app removes it: a soft status fill with the matching text colour (like Badge), an icon per tone so colour is never the only signal, an optional title, an action and a close button. role="status" (polite) by default, role="alert" only for tone="danger" with urgent. It never takes the focus; closing moves the focus to the control before the alert, so it does not fall to <body> when the alert leaves the page (see known limits).

h.p: The types are in components/feedback/Alert.d.ts. The card: components/feedback/alert.card.html.
The behaviour is tested in tests/alert.e2e.test.mjs, the colour rules in tests/alert.test.mjs.

sider.p: Feedback. Something is happening and nobody knows for how long: a ring in the accent that turns. role="status" with label as visually hidden text, so a screen reader hears "Loading" where others see the ring. Under prefers-reduced-motion it stands still and pulses. With aria-hidden it is decorative next to its own text, with no role and no text. Button's loading has its own matching ring; use that inside a button.

h.p: The types are in components/feedback/Spinner.d.ts. The card: components/feedback/spinner.card.html.
The behaviour is tested in tests/laster.e2e.test.mjs, the colour rules in tests/spinner.test.mjs.

sider.p: Feedback. The shape of content that has not arrived yet: text lines, a circle (an avatar) or a rectangle (an image, a card) in --surface-3, with a shimmer that sweeps across now and then and is off under prefers-reduced-motion. Always aria-hidden: the region around it says it is loading, with aria-busy="true" and one status text, so a screen reader hears "Loading recipes" once instead of twelve grey blocks.

h.p: The types are in components/feedback/Skeleton.d.ts. The card: components/feedback/skeleton.card.html.
The behaviour is tested in tests/laster.e2e.test.mjs, the rules in the source in tests/skeleton.test.mjs.

sider.p: Feedback. Brief feedback that does not get in the way: "Task archived", with "Undo" beside it. ToastStack is the container at the bottom right and the live region (role="status", aria-live="polite"); it is in the page from the start, empty, and toasts are added to it. A Toast on its own is role="status" itself. Five tones that only change the icon and its colour, an optional action and a close button named "Lukk".

h.p: The types are in components/feedback/Toast.d.ts. The card: components/feedback/toast.card.html.

sider.p: Feedback. "Ny versjon" (new version): the notice that a new version of the app is ready. A toast built from Toast's parts, with "Oppdater" (update) and the quieter "Senere" (later), announced politely from a live region without moving focus. By default it renders its own ToastStack from the start, so the region exists before the toast arrives; open it with open. Detection is the app's, with the helper in components/feedback/oppdatering.js: startOppdatering, vedNyVersjon, oppdater and erOpptatt.

h.p: The types are in components/feedback/NyVersjon.d.ts and components/feedback/oppdatering.d.ts. The card:…
The behaviour is tested in tests/nyversjon.e2e.test.mjs, the rules in tests/nyversjon.test.mjs.

sider.p: Icon. A Lucide icon drawn inline as SVG, so it inherits currentColor and Sussi's stroke width of 1.75 (softer than Lucide's 2). The set is 101 icons in components/icon/iconData.js: 100 from Lucide and one drawn for Sussi (yarn, a ball of yarn). Decorative by default (aria-hidden); with title it is a named image. A name that is not in the set renders nothing.

h.p: The types are in components/icon/Icon.d.ts. The card with the whole set: components/icon/icon.card.html.

sider.p: Inputs. A single-line text input with label, hint and error built in. The input is a native <input> in a frame (.s-control) that shows focus, error and disabled; the label is a <label> that points at the input; the hint, or the error when there is one, is linked with aria-describedby, and an error sets aria-invalid and is announced. mode says what the field is for (a number, an email, a phone, a date, a password …) and sets the right type, keyboard on a phone and autofill; a password gets a show/hide toggle. Field is the same label/hint/error anatomy around a control you build yourself.

h.p: The types are in components/inputs/Input.d.ts. The card with Input, Textarea and Select:…
Your own type, inputMode, autoComplete or enterKeyHint wins over the table. Without mode nothing is set, as before.
The links are tested in tests/forms.e2e.test.mjs.

sider.p: Inputs. Two to five mutually exclusive options in a row, as one value in a form. Underneath it is a native radio group: a <fieldset role="radiogroup"> with a <legend> that names the group, and one visually hidden <input type="radio"> per option inside a <label>, so the browser gives the keyboard for free: one Tab stop, the arrow keys move and check within the group. The look is the same track as Tabs variant="segmented", but the role is another: Tabs switch what is shown, SegmentedControl answers a question.

h.p: The types are in components/inputs/SegmentedControl.d.ts. The card: components/inputs/segmentedcontrol.card.html.
The behaviour is tested in tests/segmentedcontrol.e2e.test.mjs, the rules in tests/segmentedcontrol.test.mjs.

sider.p: Inputs. A group of related controls, above all a radio or checkbox group: a native <fieldset> with a <legend> that names the group, an optional hint under the legend and an error under the controls, both tied to the group with aria-describedby. The error carries an icon and text and is announced (role="alert"), so colour is never the only signal; the group also gets a --danger edge on the left. The children are the existing Radio, Checkbox and Switch, unchanged.

h.p: The types are in components/inputs/Fieldset.d.ts. The card: components/inputs/fieldset.card.html.
The behaviour is tested in tests/fieldset.e2e.test.mjs, the rules in tests/fieldset.test.mjs.

sider.p: Inputs. A native dropdown with the same label, hint, error and frame as Input. options are strings or { value, label }, placeholder adds a first empty option, and the chevron on the right is drawn by Sussi while the list that opens is the browser's own. For five or more options; fewer is Radio or segmented Tabs.

h.p: The types are in components/inputs/Select.d.ts. The card: components/inputs/inputs.card.html.
The links are tested in tests/forms.e2e.test.mjs.

sider.p: Inputs. A multi-line text input for notes and descriptions, with the same label, hint and error as Input. A native <textarea> with four visible lines by default (rows), at least 88 px tall, and resizable vertically.

h.p: The types are in components/inputs/Textarea.d.ts. The card: components/inputs/inputs.card.html.
The links are tested in tests/forms.e2e.test.mjs (the hint and an app's own aria-describedby are tested on a Textarea).

sider.p: Display. A section that shows and hides: native <details> and <summary>, so the browser gives the button role, aria-expanded, Enter and Space, and the content is in the page whether the section is open or not. The row is 44 px tall with the title and a chevron that turns when the section opens, on --dur-base, which is 0 under reduced motion. Uncontrolled with defaultOpen, or controlled with open and onToggle. One section at a time; a list of sections is several Disclosures after each other, not an accordion.

h.p: The types are in components/display/Disclosure.d.ts. The card: components/display/disclosure.card.html.
The behaviour is tested in tests/disclosure.e2e.test.mjs, the rules in tests/disclosure.test.mjs.

sider.p: Navigation. Tabs switch between sibling views: underline for sections of a page, segmented for view switches and filters. The keyboard follows the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern: only the selected tab is in the Tab order, ← and → move and select, Home and End jump to the ends. TabPanels as children are wired to their tab with aria-controls and aria-labelledby, and the panels not shown stay mounted, so what you typed survives a switch. Controlled (value) or not (defaultValue).

h.p: The types are in components/navigation/Tabs.d.ts. The card: components/navigation/tabs.card.html.
Plus every attribute of <div> (React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>).
The behaviour is tested in tests/tabs.e2e.test.mjs.

sider.p: Navigation. The frame around an app, with its main menu: a tab bar at the bottom below 900 px and a 248 px sidebar from 900 px, both <nav aria-label="Hovedmeny"> with aria-current="page" on the item you are on. Up to five tabs fit; with more, the fifth becomes "Mer" (more), a keyboard-usable list of the rest. AppShell renders the page's <main> with room for the tab bar and the home indicator, and the first thing in the tab order is a skip link to <main>. contained gives the tab bar at every width, at the bottom of the app's own frame.

h.p: The types are in components/navigation/AppShell.d.ts. The card: components/navigation/appshell.card.html.
The behaviour is tested in tests/appshell.e2e.test.mjs and tests/appshell-hover.e2e.test.mjs, the rules in…

sider.p: Navigation. A link: the accent text colour (--accent-text) and the underline base.css already gives every <a>, plus the variants. inline sits in running text and wraps with it; standalone is a link on its own line, in medium weight and at least 24 px tall. With target="blank" the link says so: rel="noopener noreferrer", an external icon and the visually hidden «(åpner i ny fane)», so a screen reader hears where it goes. as takes a router's Link, so the app keeps client-side routing.

h.p: The types are in components/navigation/Link.d.ts. The card: components/navigation/link.card.html.
The behaviour is tested in tests/link.e2e.test.mjs, the colour rules in tests/link.test.mjs.

sider.p: Navigation. "Back": a Link on its own line with a chevron before the text, at the top of a page that was opened from another: a plant from the list, a day from the week. It is Link, so href, or as with to for a router, and the ref reach the <a>; standalone gives the medium weight and at least 24 px of height. The text defaults to «Tilbake» and names the place when that helps: "Back to plants".

h.p: The types are in components/navigation/BackLink.d.ts. The card: components/navigation/backlink.card.html.
The behaviour is tested in tests/backlink.e2e.test.mjs, the rules in tests/backlink.test.mjs; the colour is Link's…

sider.p: Layout. A layout primitive: the children in a column (default) or a row, with a gap from the spacing tokens (gap={4} is --space-4, 16 px), optional wrap and alignment. Flex with the gap as a custom property, so the CSS is one rule and the step is always a token. Nothing visual of its own and no role: a surface is a Card, a frame is AppShell.

h.p: The types are in components/layout/Stack.d.ts. The card: components/layout/layout.card.html.
The behaviour is tested in tests/layout.e2e.test.mjs, the rules in tests/stack.test.mjs.

sider.p: Layout. Text for assistive technology that nobody sees: the .s-sr-only class as a component. The element is 1 px, clipped and out of the flow, never display:none or visibility:hidden, so a screen reader reads it and role="status" on it is announced. focusable is for a skip link or another control that must show when it has the focus: it then comes back into the flow where it stands in the document, at least 24 px tall. AppShell has its own skip link; this is for pages without it.

h.p: The types are in components/layout/VisuallyHidden.d.ts. The card: components/layout/layout.card.html.
The behaviour is tested in tests/layout.e2e.test.mjs, the rules in tests/visuallyhidden.test.mjs.

sider.p: Utilities. Dates the Norwegian way, and the English way for English surfaces: functions without a framework and without dependencies, on Intl.DateTimeFormat with nb-NO and en-GB, so the month names and the order come from the browser. formatDato gives «30. okt. 2026» or «30. oktober 2026» (en "30 Oct 2026", "30 October 2026"), formatRelativ "today", "yesterday" and "tomorrow", formatTid "14:30" and formatTidsrom "14:30–15:15". A date without a time ("2026-10-30", what <input type="date"> and a database date column give) is read as a local calendar day, never as midnight UTC, and days are compared on calendar dates, so a change to or from DST never moves a date.

h.p: The types are in components/utils/dato.d.ts. The card: components/utils/dato.card.html.
The helper renders nothing; what counts is the text it gives.

sider.p: Overlays. A modal dialog with a scrim, following the WAI-ARIA dialog pattern: focus moves in on open, Tab stays inside, Esc and a click on the scrim close it, and focus returns to what opened it. Named by title and described by description; the page behind is locked against scrolling. variant="sheet" is the same dialog risen from the bottom of the screen (full width on a phone, 560 px centred on a bigger screen, a grab handle, the body scrolling inside), and portal renders it in <body> so a positioned parent cannot draw over it.

h.p: The types are in components/overlays/Dialog.d.ts. The cards: components/overlays/overlays.card.html (the dialog) and…
The behaviour is tested in tests/dialog.e2e.test.mjs and tests/sheet.e2e.test.mjs, the rules in tests/sheet.test.mjs.

sider.p: Overlays. A short label shown on hover and focus, after 300 ms, for icon buttons and shortcuts. The bubble is linked to the trigger with aria-describedby, the trigger's native title is removed so there is only one bubble, Esc hides the bubble without moving the mouse or focus, and the mouse can move from the trigger onto the bubble without it closing (WCAG 1.4.13). kbd shows a keyboard shortcut in monospace.

h.p: The types are in components/overlays/Tooltip.d.ts. The card, shared with Dialog: components/overlays/overlays.card.html.
The behaviour is tested in tests/tooltip.e2e.test.mjs.

sider.p: Overlays. A non-modal surface anchored to the button that opens it. The button gets aria-expanded and aria-controls and toggles the panel on click; the panel sits below the button (above with side="top"), flips when it does not fit and there is more room on the other side, and stays 8 px inside the viewport, also at 320 px. Focus moves in on open, Esc closes with focus back on the button, a click outside and focus moving elsewhere close it, and Tab at the panel's edge goes back through the button, so the page's tab order carries on from there. Menu is a Popover with role="menu"; use that for a list of actions.

h.p: The types are in components/overlays/Popover.d.ts. The card: components/overlays/menu.card.html (the menu and a…
The behaviour is tested in tests/popover.e2e.test.mjs, the rules and the placement in tests/popover.test.mjs.

sider.p: Overlays. A menu button following the WAI-ARIA menu button pattern: a Button or IconButton with aria-haspopup="menu" that opens a list of actions in a Popover with role="menu". Enter, Space and ArrowDown open on the first item, ArrowUp on the last; the arrows move with wrap, Home and End jump, a letter goes to the next item starting with it; Enter and Space choose and close, Esc closes and puts focus back on the button, Tab closes and moves on. An item can be a link (href), checked (checked), disabled (disabled) or set apart in the danger colour (danger); '-' is a separator and { label, items } a group with a heading. Items are 44 px on touch and 32 px with a mouse.

h.p: The types are in components/overlays/Menu.d.ts. The card: components/overlays/menu.card.html. The remaining props are…
The behaviour is tested in tests/menu.e2e.test.mjs, the rules and the contrast in tests/menu.test.mjs.

sider.p: Mascot. The mascot, the cat the system is named after: white with black ears, mask, back patches and tail, and a pink nose. Always black and white, whatever the app's accent; the colours are the --sussi- tokens, and dark mode gives her a thin light halo so the black parts do not vanish. Six poses as inline SVG: hode (head: logo, favicon, avatar), ligger (lying), titter (peeking: empty states), sover (sleeping: loading), strekk (stretching: play, 404) and sitter (sitting: welcome). Decorative by default; title names her when she carries meaning alone. sussiPoses gives the SVG markup per pose for favicons and static exports.

h.p: The types are in components/mascot/Sussi.d.ts. The card: components/mascot/mascot.card.html.
The behaviour is tested in tests/mascot.e2e.test.mjs.

sider.p: Colours with measured contrast, type, spacing, radius, shadows and motion: the tokens Sussi is built from. Warm stone neutrals do almost all the work. Moss is the one accent, and five muted accent families exist for app colours. Every pair below is measured with WCAG 2 contrast from the tokens, the way npm test does it.

h.p: Warm stone neutrals do almost all the work. Moss is the one accent, and five muted accent families exist for app…
Schibsted Grotesk handles everything from UI to display, DM Mono is the technical voice: meta, numbers, keyboard hints…
The base unit is 4 px. Controls are 30, 38 and 46 px tall, cards have 20 px of padding, and the space between sections…
Soft, subtle radii: 6 px on controls, 10 px on medium containers, 14 px on cards, 20 px on dialogs, and pill on badges,…
Low, diffuse and warm. Borders carry structure; a shadow only means “lifted”. Dark mode uses deeper shadows plus a…
Calm and short: 120 ms for hover and press, 200 ms for toggles and tabs, 320 ms for dialogs and toasts. Nothing bounces.…

sider.p: Every Sussi token as JSON in the W3C format, and the table of semantic tokens in light and dark mode and every accent.

h.p: Surfaces, text, lines, accent and status, in light and dark mode. The components use only these.
What a data-accent sets, per accent and mode. Moss is the default.
Spacing, control heights, radius, durations and font sizes, the same in both modes.

sider.p: Sussi sounds like a calm, competent colleague: someone who knows psychology, respects your attention and never makes you feel stupid. These are the rules for every piece of text in a Sussi interface, Norwegian first and English as the second language. Every component has its own "Content" section in docs/komponenter/; this is the ground they build on.

h.p: The pattern: what happened + what to do now. Never blame, never codes, never exclamation marks.
An empty list is not an error. Say what is empty, then one next step, then at most one action.
Undo beats "Are you sure?". What can be reversed happens at once, and a toast offers "Undo". A dialog is used only for…
Feedback after every action, quietly: "Saved", "Task archived", "Copied". Past tense, one line, no "Success!". A form…
The common words in an interface, as Sussi uses them. The same word for the same thing across the app.

sider.p: The 101 icons in Sussi, from Lucide, with search. The Lucide set, drawn at stroke 1.75 through Icon. yarn was drawn for Sussi. Icons inherit currentColor; pair them with a label in navigation, and give icon buttons a name.

Pick an accent colour and get a whole Sussi theme with the contrast checked in light and dark. A preview on real components, the report, CSS and JSON. One colour in, a whole theme out. The engine (tokens/tema.js) derives the accent group in OKLCH (a colour space where lightness is an axis of its own, so it can move without the hue shifting) and moves lightness only until every pair holds the requirement Sussi puts on its own accents. What you set yourself never moves. Everything runs here in the browser.

Every rule the engine holds, with the measured ratio. Moved says what was adjusted and why.
